$comment: SHAPE FIXTURE, NOT A VENDOR CLAIM. Every entry below is SYNTHETIC and labelled as such in its authority field, because this repo does not ship vendor models and inventing one would put a fabricated frequency range next to a real part number (constraint #3). The point of the fixture is to exercise the four gates - integrity, supersession, envelope, authority - not to assert anything about any manufacturer's silicon. A real registry replaces these with vendor_published entries whose provenance names an actual document and revision.

models.notes: Generated by this repo to exercise the machinery. It produces real numbers and can never open a sign-off gate - that is the whole reason the synthetic tier exists rather than being folded into vendor_derived.

provenance.document: digitised from a synthetic response, not a datasheet

models.notes: Two axes on purpose: rail_budget.py refuses a PSRR figure quoted at another frequency, and this is the machine-readable form of that refusal. The temperature axis exists so a query at 125 degC is OUT_OF_ENVELOPE rather than silently answered.
Present only so the supersession gate has something to refuse: synthetic-pair-10g declares it obsolete, and a query naming this id must FAIL rather than come back with a note attached.
